title.narrative: Operational response and management of the rule of law at sea

description.narrative: This Actions overall objective is strengthen law enforcement operational capacities and responses, which corresponds to SWAIMS second outcome . It seeks to address the causes for the lack of a steady and effective operational coordination in regards to intelligence between law enforcement agencies of the GoG at all levels (national, regional and inter-regional). Thus, law enforcement bodies will be provided with resources and technical assistance not only to improve the exchange of information related to maritime surveillance, but also to reinforce cooperation among them and with other key stakeholders (e.g. CSOs and private sector). Furthermore, those agencies will also be provided with equipment and training to improve their interventions at sea, which is the focus of this Action. The impact of the Action will be assessed by the extent to which law enforcement operational capacities and responses have been strengthened and how this has, as a result, contributed to improve maritime security and safety in the Gulf of Guinea in the ECOWAS region the integrated programme overall objective. Outcome: The outcome of this Action is that operational response and management of the rule of law at sea are improved through the supply of fast response and forensic equipment. It aims at addressing the need for naval forces of ECOWAS countries to deploy law enforcement officers and increase their capacity to intervene at sea to respond timely to maritime incidents (including environmental crimes), through the provision of RHIB/RBBs, forensic equipment and operational training. By the end of this Action all RHIB/RBBs and forensic equipment are expected to have been supplied to the eligible selected ECOWAS countries. These countries will also have their crews and law enforcement teams trained and ready to operate at sea, conducting boarding operations and inspections effectively, all security measures accounted for. Furthermore, the countries that receive RHIB/RBBs and its forensic equipment will have an increased logistics and maintenance capacity that meets a level deemed appropriate to ensure mid to long term sustainability.
